title: Three reaction types and what defines them
body: Identify a reaction as acid-base, oxidation-reduction (redox), or precipitation by what is transferred or formed.

items.label: Acid-base
items.meaning: Transfer of one or more protons (H+ ions) between chemical species.

items.label: Oxidation-reduction (redox)
items.meaning: Transfer of one or more electrons between chemical species, shown by changes in oxidation numbers; electrons go from the species oxidized to the species reduced. Combustion is a redox subclass, and complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives CO2 and H2O.

items.label: Precipitation
items.meaning: Mixing ions in aqueous solution produces an insoluble or sparingly soluble ionic compound. All sodium, potassium, ammonium, and nitrate salts are soluble.

title: Building a balanced redox equation from half-reactions
body: Write the oxidation and reduction half-reactions and combine them into one balanced redox equation that conserves atoms and charge.
caution: In the oxidation half-reaction, electrons appear as a product. Do not omit them, and do not write the reduction direction for a species identified as oxidized (e.g., at the anode).
ced_evidence: 4.9.A.1 Balanced chemical equations for redox reactions can be constructed from half-reactions.
